propositions.text: Mr. Momcilo Rudan seeks judicial review of Officer CNC's March 16, 2021 decision refusing his employer-specific work permit.
propositions.quote: The Applicant, Mr. Momcilo Rudan, seeks judicial review of the decision of Officer CNC at the Case processing Centre Edmonton, dated March 16, 2021, and refusing his application for an employer-specific work permit.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Mr. Rudan seeks judicial review of the March 16, 2021 decision refusing his employer-specific work permit.

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan confirms only the employer-specific work permit refusal is before the Court, not the open work permit refusal.
propositions.quote: Mr. Rudan confirmed that the only decision for which leave had been granted, and which is thus properly before the Court in these proceedings, is the one refusing his employer-specific work permit.

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan confirms the open work permit refusal decision is not before the Court.
propositions.quote: Mr. Rudan confirmed as well that the other decision rendered the same day, refusing his application for an open work permit, is not before the Court in these proceedings.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Rudan confirms only the employer-specific work permit refusal is before the Court, not the open work permit refusal.

propositions.text: The Officer refused Mr. Rudan's work permit application under subsection 205(b) based on lack of evidence of reciprocity and exchange agreement.
propositions.quote: the Officer refused the application Mr. Rudan had presented for a work permit under subsection 205(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations... based on reciprocity. The Officer considered that Mr. Rudan had failed to provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate that reciprocity existed and had failed to provide sufficient proof of an exchange agreement

paragraphs.summary: The Officer refused Mr. Rudan's work permit application under subsection 205(b) due to insufficient evidence of reciprocity and exchange agreement.

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan has not met his burden to show the Officer's decision is unreasonable.
propositions.quote: I find that Mr. Rudan has not met his burden to convince me that the Officer’s decision is unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Mr. Rudan has not met his burden to show the Officer's decision is unreasonable.

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan is a Serbian citizen and professional soccer player who had a work permit valid until October 10, 2020, and applied for new permits on October 5, 2020.
propositions.quote: Mr. Rudan is a citizen of the Republic of Serbia and a professional soccer player. On October 15, 2019, he obtained a work permit... valid until October 10, 2020. On October 5, 2020, he applied for new work permits.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Mr. Rudan is a Serbian soccer player who had a work permit valid until October 10, 2020, and applied for new permits on October 5, 2020.

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan sought to extend his work permit to continue playing for Scarborough Soccer Club and cited LMIA Exemption Code C-20 and subsection 205(a).
propositions.quote: Mr. Rudan indicated that he was looking to extend his work permit to continue playing soccer for the Scarborough Soccer Club... cited the Citizenship and Immigration Canada guidelines regarding Labour Market Impact Assessment [LMIA] Exemption Code C-20 relating to reciprocity, adopted under subsection 205(b) of the Regulations, and cited subsection 205(a) of the Regulations.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Rudan sought to extend his work permit to continue playing for Scarborough Soccer Club, citing LMIA Exemption Code C-20 and subsection 205(a).

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan presented only written submissions about two Canadian players in Serbia and Wikipedia pages as evidence of reciprocity.
propositions.quote: Mr. Rudan presented only (1) written submissions that two Canadian players played for Serbia; and (2) primarily Wikipedia pages concerning these two players and the Canadian and Serbian football leagues, as well as profiles of the two Canadian players available on the Internet.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Rudan presented only written submissions about two Canadian players in Serbia and Wikipedia pages as evidence of reciprocity.

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan argues the Officer's reasons are inadequate, unreasonable, and confused, lacking explanation of how the conclusion was reached.
propositions.quote: Mr. Rudan takes issue with the adequacy of the Officer’s reasons... said reasons disclose an unreasonable and confused decision... disclosed nothing as to how they... had arrived at this conclusion.

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan argues the Officer's reasons do not sufficiently explain what was missing and should have requested missing information or relied on prior permit issuance.
propositions.quote: the Officer should have explained more in details what was missing, could have reached out to request what was missing, and could have relied on the fact that a prior work permit had been issued in the same category

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan cites Supreme Court paragraphs 96 and 97 in Vavilov on adequacy of reasons.
propositions.quote: Mr. Rudan cites paragraphs 96 and 97 of the Supreme Court of Canada’s decision in Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 on the adequacy of reasons.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Rudan argues the Officer's reasons are inadequate, unreasonable, and confused, citing Vavilov paragraphs 96 and 97, and should have explained missing evidence or requested it.

propositions.text: The Minister argues the decision is reasonable and the reasons are sufficient and adequate.
propositions.quote: The Minister essentially responds that the decision is reasonable, and that the reasons are sufficient and adequate.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the Minister that the decision is reasonable and reasons adequate.
propositions.quote: Given the circumstances of this case, I agree.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argues the decision is reasonable and reasons adequate; the court agrees.

propositions.text: Reasons must be clear, precise, intelligible so applicants understand why applications failed and can seek review.
propositions.quote: reasons are required to be sufficiently clear, precise and intelligible so that an applicant may know why his or her application failed and be able to decide whether to seek judicial review.

propositions.text: Visa officer decisions need not be comprehensive but must be comprehensible and justify the outcome in context (citing cases).
propositions.quote: Decisions of a visa officer need not be comprehensive and may be brief or limited provided that the reasons are comprehensible... must justify why these circumstances led to a particular outcome (Zhu v Canada... Musadiq v Canada... Ogunfowora v Canada... Peiro v Canada... Hajiyeva v Canada).

paragraphs.summary: The court states reasons must be clear and intelligible; visa officer decisions may be brief but must justify outcomes, citing case law.

propositions.text: The Officer's reasons clearly informed Mr. Rudan that his evidence was insufficient to establish reciprocity, including lack of exchange agreement.
propositions.quote: the Officer’s reasons are short, but clearly informs Mr. Rudan that the documentation he submitted... was insufficient to establish that the required reciprocity existed... This evidence includes providing and exchange agreement, as noted by the Officer, which was not provided here.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer's reasons clearly informed Mr. Rudan his evidence was insufficient to establish reciprocity, including lack of exchange agreement.

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan does not argue evidence was ignored or sufficient; given little evidence, the Officer's decision is reasonable.
propositions.quote: Mr. Rudan does not argue before the Court that the evidence before the Officer was ignored or that it was sufficient to established reciprocity... the Officer’s decision is reasonable.

propositions.text: Insufficient evidence was adduced; no authority requires Officer to detail missing evidence or provide more detailed reasons.
propositions.quote: Not much could be said except that insufficient evidence had been adduced... Mr. Rudan has filed no authorities for the proposition that the Officer must provide more details as to what was missing for the applicant to have met his burden, and for the reasons to be adequate.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Mr. Rudan does not argue evidence was ignored; given insufficient evidence, the Officer's decision is reasonable and no authority requires more detailed reasons.

propositions.text: Mr. Rudan failed to establish reasons are inadequate; judicial review application is dismissed with no costs or questions certified.
propositions.quote: Mr. Rudan has failed to establish that the reasons are inadequate given the record. The application for judicial review will be dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes Mr. Rudan failed to show reasons are inadequate; judicial review is dismissed with no costs or questions certified.
